assessment: How the pathogens Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus compete and co-occur within opportunistic infections is an important problem, but the major drivers of these interactions remain unclear. Here the authors contribute a fundamental advance by defining parameters that predict the coexistence of these microbes using their absolute growth in various nutritional conditions, which could explain the dominance of one or the other during infections. Within a defined context, this valuable study provides solid support for a novel framework in which to evaluate this clinically important species interaction.
